title.value: Fine-tuning Happens in Tiny Subspaces: Exploring Intrinsic Task-specific Subspaces of Pre-trained Language Models
title.justification: The paper focuses on the fine-tuning process in pre-trained language models (PLMs), particularly exploring task-specific subspaces.
title.quote: In this paper, we study the problem of re-parameterizing and fine-tuning PLMs from a new perspective: Discovery of intrinsic task-specific subspace.

extractions.description: This paper studies the fine-tuning of pre-trained language models (PLMs) in task-specific subspaces. By analyzing the fine-tuning trajectory, the authors aim to uncover small, task-specific subspaces within PLMs where fine-tuning can effectively occur. The study demonstrates that effective task adaptation can happen in these limited dimensions, and experiments on models like BERT and RoBERTa show promising results. The paper further explores the presence and impact of outlier dimensions during this process.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on optimizing language models, specifically through task-specific subspaces within PLMs, without addressing direct climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this paper, we study the problem of re-parameterizing and fine-tuning PLMs from a new perspective: Discovery of intrinsic task-specific subspace.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development. Its primary focus is on improving the efficiency of language model fine-tuning.
primary_category.quote: Despite the great success of this paradigm, two questions still come to our mind: (1) Why can a PLM with hundreds of millions of parameters be successfully fine-tuned on different downstream tasks using only hundreds or thousands of labeled samples? (2) Do we really need a full fine-tuning of all parameters of a PLM to reach state-of-the-art performance on downstream tasks?

secondary_categories.justification: No additional categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development are addressed in the paper.
secondary_categories.quote: We interpret the ease of adapting PLMs to downstream tasks as fine-tuning happens in tiny intrinsic task-specific subspaces.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus of the paper is on language model parameter optimization, which does not fit within any defined climate or ecological sub-categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: To uncover such intrinsic task-specific subspaces, we exploit the fine-tuning trajectory to find its main direction.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological themes because the paper focuses on machine learning model efficiency rather than sustainability.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The ease of adapting PLMs to downstream tasks is explained by the existence of intrinsic task-specific subspaces.

new_primary_category.justification: The study pertains to machine learning model optimization without any emphasis on sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose a method to uncover the subspaces by finding the principal directions of the fine-tuning trajectory.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new category or sub-category related to climate or ecological sustainable development is identified through this research.
